kept.name: qwen38-27b-200k-on-16gb
kept.reason: Step-by-step recipe for running Qwen 3.8 27B at about 196K context on one 16 GB GPU, with KV paging into host RAM. This is the brief's exact setup.

kept.name: llama-cpp-adaptive-kv-streaming
kept.reason: llama.cpp fork that streams the KV cache from host RAM, letting Qwen3.8-27B use its full 256K context on 16 GB of VRAM. It is the engine the 16 GB recipe relies on.

kept.name: large-moe-consumer-hardware
kept.reason: Guide to running Qwen3.8 MoE models with experts held in system RAM and attention on a 16 GB GPU (--cpu-moe), plus KV cache sizing at 262K context. It fits the 16 GB GPU + 64 GB RAM setup.

kept.name: strata
kept.reason: One-click engine for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on 12–24 GB consumer NVIDIA cards, moving experts between GPU, RAM and SSD. It covers both the 16 GB and the 24 GB tier.

kept.name: freetoken
kept.reason: MoE inference engine that keeps experts in system RAM and caches the active ones on the GPU, and reuses saved context across agent turns. It has an Anthropic-compatible API and suits a GPU that's too small for the whole model.

kept.name: kv-cache-vram-sizing
kept.reason: Formula for working out KV cache memory, so you can see how much context fits on a 16, 24 or 48 GB card. This is central when long context matters most.

kept.name: turboquant
kept.reason: 3–4 bit KV cache compression that stretches how much context fits in limited VRAM.

kept.name: qwopus38-27b-flash
kept.reason: Efficiency-tuned Qwen3.8-27B GGUF aimed at agent workloads: less runaway reasoning and better multi-token prediction (MTP) acceptance. A candidate model for 24 GB and larger cards.

kept.name: qwen3-6-27b
kept.reason: Open-weight 27B coding model with 262K context. It's a local worker candidate, though it needs quantization to fit.

kept.name: qwen3-8-27b-uncensored-hauhaucs-aggressive-gguf
kept.reason: Community GGUF builds of Qwen3.8-27B at several quant levels, with a speculative-decoding (MTP) add-on. It shows which sizes fit at 16, 24 or 48 GB, but its safety behavior has been stripped, so use with care.

kept.name: ornith-dgx-spark-setup
kept.reason: Setup for a 35B MoE model (3B active) with 262K context, using an approximately 22 GiB NVFP4 checkpoint. A plausible model and vLLM setup for a 48 GB card.

kept.name: local-model-picks-2026
kept.reason: Practitioner list of local models with their memory needs, including coding picks. Useful for choosing a model at each size.

kept.name: llmfit
kept.reason: Detects your GPU, RAM and VRAM and scores which models and context lengths will run well. Directly helps pick a model at each hardware size.

kept.name: lm-studio
kept.reason: Desktop app that estimates whether a model fits in VRAM, gives GPU offload controls, and serves an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API. An easy way to get set up.

kept.name: unsloth
kept.reason: Publisher of the GGUF quants the recipes use, and offers an API endpoint for Claude Code and Codex.

kept.name: claude-code-local-model-switching
kept.reason: How to point Claude Code at a local Ollama or LM Studio server, including a KV cache fix and a Qwen config. The step that connects a local model to agentic coding.

kept.name: local-model-harness-patterns
kept.reason: Harness design patterns for running local models as coding agents: subagents, loop detection, speculative decoding.

kept.name: local-model-adversarial-workflow
kept.reason: Workflow where a local Qwen 27B drafts and implements while cloud models review. A practical way to use a local model that can't do everything alone.

kept.name: gvs5h-ledger-orchestration
kept.reason: Shows Qwen3.8-27B's coding scores rising a lot when the task is broken into steps that share notes through files. A useful strategy for getting more out of a local model.

kept.name: state-of-open-coding-models-2026
kept.reason: A useful caution: the strongest open coding models no longer fit consumer hardware, so expectations at the 16–48 GB sizes need adjusting.

kept.name: on-prem-llm-deployment-architecture
kept.reason: Covers hardware and inference-stack choices (llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama) with memory sizing. Relevant when moving to a 24 or 48 GB card.

kept.name: qwen25-coder-32b
kept.reason: Older code-specialized 32B Qwen with 128K context. Its few KV heads keep the cache small, making it a baseline coding model for 24–48 GB cards.

kept.name: contextual-retrieval-anthropic
kept.reason: Canonical hybrid recipe (contextual embeddings + contextual BM25 + reranking) with measured gains — the closest benchmark for lexical-plus-semantic retrieval.

kept.name: three-store-hybrid-memory-architecture
kept.reason: Agent memory built from a vector store, an exact-lookup store and a knowledge graph merged by a fusion layer — a direct analogue of typed records plus a graph plus embeddings.

kept.name: titans-atlas-cronus
kept.reason: Persistent project memory with a typed graph, where retrieval blends lexical, vector, graph and evidence signals — very close to your design.

kept.name: okf-agent-memory
kept.reason: Git-native Markdown+YAML knowledge bundle for coding agents searched with in-memory BM25 over MCP — the lexical-only version of your approach.

kept.name: gbrain
kept.reason: Persistent typed records with relationships plus vector/semantic search — a near-identical system to compare against.

kept.name: mempalace
kept.reason: Local-first agent memory with a knowledge graph, semantic search, Claude Code integration and published R@5 benchmarks to compare with.

kept.name: claude-mem
kept.reason: Claude Code memory that adds SQLite + Chroma vector search; the catalog's note that it adds complexity without clear benefit is a useful lesson.

kept.name: memoose
kept.reason: Local memory for coding agents built on a SQLite knowledge graph — a graph-first approach to compare with yours.

kept.name: tencentdb-agent-memory
kept.reason: Team memory hub with linked wiki pages, BM25 and vector retrieval — covers similar ground at team scale.

kept.name: tolvi
kept.reason: Markdown decision vault for agents with CAG/RAG dual-mode retrieval — the same problem space as typed records.

kept.name: synapse-memory-layer
kept.reason: Structured memory atoms with embeddings in pgvector behind a write-quality gate — another typed-record-plus-vectors design.

kept.name: fluxmem
kept.reason: Research memory architecture that treats memory as an evolving linked graph of typed nodes — conceptual comparison for the graph side.

kept.name: ai-memory-comparison
kept.reason: Source-backed survey of 73 agent memory systems across 79 features — the broadest view for placing your approach.

kept.name: agentic-memory-benchmark
kept.reason: Benchmark in which a plain curated markdown wiki beat commercial memory products — direct evidence for your markdown-first approach.

kept.name: kb
kept.reason: Your own repo-local wiki and deterministic graph toolkit — the baseline the other results are being compared against.

kept.name: open-knowledge-format
kept.reason: Google spec for Markdown+frontmatter agent knowledge with provenance/freshness signals and a graph view — a format peer to typed markdown records.

kept.name: karpathy-llm-wiki
kept.reason: Foundational pattern for LLM-maintained markdown wikis as an alternative to RAG — the design lineage for your approach.

kept.name: agentic-rag-terminal-tools
kept.reason: Evidence that grep/terminal tools beat embedding retrieval for agents — a key counterpoint before you commit to embeddings.

kept.name: sira-superintelligent-retrieval-agent
kept.reason: Shows LLM-enriched documents and queries let plain BM25 beat dense retrievers — a way to boost lexical search without vectors.

kept.name: sira
kept.reason: Code release of the SIRA enrichment-plus-BM25 pipeline, for trying lexical enrichment directly.

kept.name: rag-architecture-decision-tree
kept.reason: Framework for choosing hybrid, reranked, graph or agentic RAG based on observed failures; also recommends measuring retrieval separately from generation.

kept.name: production-rag-system-taxonomy
kept.reason: System view of RAG that includes retrieval evals and observability (recall, freshness), useful for checking what your design is missing.

kept.name: rag-retrieval-recipe
kept.reason: Practitioner baseline RAG pipeline (embed, retrieve top-20, rerank, cite) to compare with.

kept.name: agentic-rag
kept.reason: Pattern where the agent reformulates queries and iterates retrieval — relevant because your consumers are agents.

kept.name: graphrag-agent-memory-linkedin-series
kept.reason: Conceptual grounding on GraphRAG and unified agent memory, for the graph-plus-retrieval combination.

kept.name: pageindex
kept.reason: Vectorless retrieval that has an LLM reason over a hierarchical tree index — an alternative to adding embeddings.

kept.name: chunkless-rag
kept.reason: Retrieval that keeps document structure and navigates by section summaries — relevant to structured markdown records.

kept.name: pdf-mcp
kept.reason: Small local MCP server with BM25 + semantic hybrid search and a SQLite cache — a compact implementation reference.

kept.name: skill-search-mcp
kept.reason: Vector search over a small corpus of short agent-facing descriptions with reported recall@3 — similar scale and use case.

kept.name: lancedb
kept.reason: Embedded, in-process store with vector indexes plus BM25 full-text — a good fit for adding hybrid search locally.

kept.name: chromadb
kept.reason: Embedding-agnostic store with vector, full-text and hybrid search — a common local backend option.

kept.name: chroma
kept.reason: Chroma's open-source repo entry: simple core API with metadata filtering and in-memory or persistent modes — a lightweight local embeddings backend.

kept.name: qdrant
kept.reason: Hybrid dense/sparse search with RRF/DBSF fusion and an in-process Edge variant — a reference for fusion choices.

kept.name: weaviate
kept.reason: Vector database with semantic + BM25 hybrid search and built-in reranking — a reference for how hybrid search is usually exposed.

kept.name: milvus
kept.reason: Dense + sparse + BM25 hybrid search; its embedded Milvus Lite mode is relevant for local use.

kept.name: pgvector
kept.reason: Shows hybrid search done by combining vector similarity with Postgres full-text search, if your records move into SQL.

kept.name: embeddinggemma-2
kept.reason: Small on-device text+code embedding model with Matryoshka truncation — a candidate for the semantic layer.

kept.name: ann-index-methods
kept.reason: Cheat sheet showing flat exact search is right under 100K vectors — likely all you need at your record count.

kept.name: vector-distance-metrics-cheatsheet
kept.reason: Practical metric choice (cosine vs dot product) and Matryoshka dimension cuts for your new embedding layer.

kept.name: redis-iris
kept.reason: Commercial agent context-and-memory platform combining retrieval and long-term memory — an industry reference point for comparison.

kept.name: knowledge-graph-construction-anthropic
kept.reason: Graph-based retrieval with multi-hop queries and citations — a contrast with your deterministic graph used for retrieval.

kept.name: godogen
kept.reason: Agent workflow that builds whole games in Godot, Bevy or Babylon.js with Claude Code and calls asset-generation APIs (Gemini, Grok, Tripo3D). The closest end-to-end fit for vibe coding a 3D game.

kept.name: aaa-quality-gate-orchestration
kept.reason: Multi-agent game-dev prompt setup that checks screenshots and uses a critic agent. Covers 3D, procedural generation, art and audio generation.

kept.name: img2threejs
kept.reason: Turns a single reference image into an animation-ready Three.js 3D model. Directly useful for making game art.

kept.name: threejs-skills
kept.reason: Three.js skills for Claude Code covering geometry, materials, lighting, animation and shaders. Useful if the game runs in a browser.

kept.name: procedura
kept.reason: Text-to-3D pipeline that outputs editable models with PBR materials and exports through Blender/USD. Another way to generate props.

kept.name: mapgen4
kept.reason: Procedural wilderness map generator (elevation, rivers, biomes). A good reference for building survival-game terrain.

kept.name: markov-junior
kept.reason: Rule-based procedural generator (includes wave function collapse) for dungeons, buildings and 3D grids. Fits procedural level building.

kept.name: shan-shui-inf
kept.reason: Noise-based procedural landscapes with a strong art style. Shows how to make procedurally generated scenery look cozy.

kept.name: comfyui
kept.reason: Node-based pipeline for generating images, audio and 3D, with an API mode. Can produce textures, concept art and sound.

kept.name: localai
kept.reason: Runs image, TTS and audio generation locally behind OpenAI-compatible APIs. A cheap way to generate assets.

kept.name: huggingface-inference-providers
kept.reason: One API for image-generation and speech models from many providers. A service for asset generation.

kept.name: voicestudio
kept.reason: Local voice design and TTS with an MCP server agents can call. Useful for NPC voices and narration.

kept.name: emdly
kept.reason: Skill marketplace that includes gaming skills (balance review, playtest triage).

kept.name: spacetimedb
kept.reason: Real-time game backend behind the BitCraft survival MMO. Worth knowing about if the game gets co-op or multiplayer.

kept.name: cli-anything
kept.reason: Generates CLIs agents can drive from existing tools, e.g. Blender or game-engine tooling, so the agent can operate them during asset creation.

kept.name: awesome-claude-code-subagents
kept.reason: Subagent collection that includes game-development and game-design specialist agents.

kept.name: build-your-own-x
kept.reason: Step-by-step tutorials, including building game engines and voxel/3D games. Good grounding for a first-time game dev.

kept.name: vibe-coding-practitioner-habits
kept.reason: Advice for a beginner vibe coder: plan first, work in small pieces, and understand the generated code.

kept.name: field-guide-to-fable-finding-unknowns
kept.reason: Techniques (interviews, references, rough mockups) for nailing down a game spec before generating lots of code and assets.

kept.name: playwright-cli
kept.reason: Lets the agent take screenshots in a browser, so it can check its own work visually on a web-based Three.js/Babylon game.

kept.name: zoetrope
kept.reason: This is the tool you meant. It's a Rust TUI that reads Claude Code JSONL transcripts and shows agents and subagents live as flow graphs, with status, tool calls, timings and gaps. It also runs in the browser.

kept.name: pixel-agents
kept.reason: A live view of coding agents that shows what each one is doing (editing, reading, waiting for input). It gets this from Claude Code hooks or transcript heuristics and runs as a VS Code extension or a CLI.

kept.name: herdr
kept.reason: A terminal multiplexer that shows many coding agents at a glance with their status. Its socket API lets you spawn panes and wait on them, which fits a dispatcher.

kept.name: orca-ade
kept.reason: Runs parallel coding agents in their own worktrees and tracks them all in one place. It's close to the 'who is running' view you want.

kept.name: codeburn
kept.reason: A local TUI and web dashboard that reads session files from Claude Code, Codex and others. It's about cost, but it reads the same session data you'd need for a live agent view.

kept.name: medley
kept.reason: Multi-agent orchestration plugin with a browser mission board for watching agent status. A close example of a web view.

kept.name: mycelium
kept.reason: A coordination server for multi-agent work queues with agent identity and a dashboard. It shows a server-side way to track who is running what.

kept.name: repowire
kept.reason: A multi-agent mesh with terminal and web dashboards for agent status across sessions. Another example of how to build the view.

kept.name: cloud-session-context-repo
kept.reason: A pattern for many parallel Claude Code sessions that includes a status feed for monitoring them and spotting stuck agents.

kept.name: builderio-skills
kept.reason: Includes an agent-watchdog skill. That's directly relevant to noticing when an agent hangs.

kept.name: agent-cost-governors
kept.reason: Lesson on stuck agents: circuit breakers that trip on retry-without-progress. Useful for deciding what counts as 'hung'.

kept.name: local-model-harness-patterns
kept.reason: Covers loop detection in agent harnesses. That's a related way to flag agents that are spinning instead of working.

kept.name: kb
kept.reason: Your own agent dispatch toolkit (by match, likely the tool in question). It's where a live view would plug in.

kept.name: textual
kept.reason: A Python TUI framework whose apps can also be served to a browser. It would let one codebase give you both the terminal view and the web page.

kept.name: claude-code-dynamic-workflows
kept.reason: Claude Code's background fan-out to subagents. Zoetrope visualizes these workflows, so it's useful context for what your view would need to show.

kept.name: multi-session-management-strategies
kept.reason: Practitioner strategies for watching 3+ concurrent agent sessions without losing track of them. Applies directly to the problem.

kept.name: remote-control
kept.reason: Built-in Claude Code feature for checking on running sessions remotely. A lightweight option before building your own view.

kept.name: claude-code-commands-reference
kept.reason: Covers built-in commands for background agents and agent status. Worth checking what Claude Code already shows before building a view.

kept.name: paddleocr
kept.reason: Covers both of your local tiers: PP-StructureV3 is a PDF-to-markdown pipeline that runs on CPU, and PaddleOCR-VL is a 0.9B vision model small enough for a 16 GB GPU.

kept.name: chandra-ocr
kept.reason: Vision model that turns PDFs into markdown or HTML, with strong math and table handling. Good small-GPU candidate for complex papers; check the modified OpenRAIL-M weights license.

kept.name: ovisocr2
kept.reason: 0.8B end-to-end page-to-markdown model (LaTeX formulas, HTML tables, figure regions) with published OmniDocBench and PureDocBench scores. Strong 16 GB GPU candidate.

kept.name: jina-ocr-v1
kept.reason: Document-to-markdown model (3.4B total, 570M active) with OmniDocBench and olmOCR-Bench scores. Also has a hosted Reader API, so it fits both the small-GPU and hosted tiers. Weights are non-commercial (CC BY-NC).

kept.name: olmocr
kept.reason: AI2's 7B PDF-to-markdown model, plus a benchmark with 7K+ test cases you could reuse to score the other approaches.

kept.name: mineru
kept.reason: Open-source parser that converts PDFs to markdown, with four quality tiers and a combined vision-model/OCR engine. It runs locally on CPU or GPU, so it can be tested at more than one tier.

kept.name: docling-mcp
kept.reason: Docling (IBM's open-source document converter) wrapped as an MCP server. Docling is a standard CPU baseline for layout and table-structure parsing.

kept.name: markitdown
kept.reason: Microsoft's lightweight PDF-to-markdown converter. Useful as the simplest CPU baseline in the comparison.

kept.name: opendataloader-pdf
kept.reason: Top-benchmarked open-source PDF parser that outputs markdown and handles formulas. The entry already flags it for piloting on bioinformatics papers.

kept.name: unstructured
kept.reason: Widely used tool that splits PDFs into elements such as titles, text and tables, with layout models and OCR. Offers both a local CPU parser and a hosted API.

kept.name: meridian
kept.reason: Reference GPU setup: Docling for layout plus Qwen3-VL on vLLM for tables, figures and formulas, with measured throughput. Useful for designing a hybrid pipeline.

kept.name: amazon-textract-textractor
kept.reason: Python wrapper around Amazon Textract. Candidate for the hosted-API tier, especially for extracting tables.

kept.name: llama-index
kept.reason: Linked to LlamaParse, LlamaIndex's commercial PDF-parsing service, which is a candidate for the hosted-API tier.

kept.name: parsebench
kept.reason: Benchmark that scores document parsers on text, formatting, tables, charts and page attribution. Directly relevant to how you score results.

kept.name: extractbench
kept.reason: Benchmark with a fixed F1 metric and no LLM judge. Gives you a lesson on how to score fairly against an LLM agent baseline.

kept.name: isaacflath-ocr-guides
kept.reason: Blog series on choosing OCR models, using vision models for OCR, quantization and pipeline design. Practical lessons for the 16 GB GPU tier.

kept.name: pdf-mcp
kept.reason: MCP server that gives an agent tools to pull tables, images and charts from PDFs and handle multi-column layouts. Relevant to how the LLM agent baseline accesses PDFs.

kept.name: seb-ocr
kept.reason: Working OCR pipeline built on Gemini, with rate limiting and caching. Useful setup patterns for the hosted-API tier.

kept.name: book-to-skill
kept.reason: Existing entry for extracting text, tables and figures from computational biology methods PDFs (mentions Docling). Close to your use case.

kept.name: armorocr
kept.reason: Qwen3-VL-8B OCR model and benchmark focused on robustness to hard or distorted inputs. Possible lesson for evaluating difficult scans and figures.

kept.name: llmfit
kept.reason: Tool that checks which models fit your hardware. Useful for choosing and sizing vision models on a 16 GB GPU.

kept.name: sglang
kept.reason: Serving framework for vision models, an alternative to vLLM. Useful for running the small vision models locally.

kept.name: kb
kept.reason: The repo-local wiki itself (MCP + CLI with search, lint and validation), so it is the system you would be benchmarking.

kept.name: okf-agent-memory
kept.reason: Closest analog: Markdown+YAML agent memory bundle with in-memory BM25 search (reports under 300µs) and a linter, so you have latency numbers and a design to compare against.

kept.name: agentic-memory-benchmark
kept.reason: Benchmark of agent memory systems (200 fact-recall tasks plus 72 never-stored hallucination checks) in which a plain markdown wiki won. Its task design can be reused to check that search finds the right records.

kept.name: mempalace
kept.reason: Local agent memory that publishes R@5 retrieval benchmarks. A reference for the metric and for what a good recall score looks like.

kept.name: skill-search-mcp
kept.reason: Measured recall@3 (0.79) over 117 short markdown descriptions with an eval harness. Similar corpus size and the same kind of retrieval-quality test.

kept.name: mex
kept.reason: Markdown agent-memory scaffold with an 11-checker drift/lint CLI. Close to kb's lint, useful for comparing which checks to time and how they grow with record count.

kept.name: agentic-rag-terminal-tools
kept.reason: Shows grep/terminal-tool retrieval beating embedding search across many benchmarks. A useful baseline to compare kb's search against as the corpus grows.

kept.name: contextual-retrieval-anthropic
kept.reason: Pass@k evaluation method for BM25/hybrid retrieval. Directly applicable to scoring search quality at each corpus size.

kept.name: building-evals-anthropic
kept.reason: How to build a golden-answer eval set and grade it with code. Covers building the ground-truth query→record set the search-quality benchmark needs.

kept.name: kb
kept.reason: This is your own repo-local wiki toolkit, with an MCP wiki, CLI and graph. It's probably the 'wiki' where you track projects.

kept.name: karpathy-llm-wiki
kept.reason: The founding pattern doc for an LLM-maintained personal knowledge base. It describes the architecture kb implements.

kept.name: obsidian-claude-second-brain-workflow
kept.reason: A working example of Claude organizing books, articles and posts into a tagged, cross-linked markdown wiki. That matches your note-saving workflow.

kept.name: third-brain-v5-wiki
kept.reason: A wiki and knowledge layer with ingest and lint steps. It also detects stale and contradicting notes, which was flagged as worth borrowing for kb.

kept.name: graphify
kept.reason: The direct inspiration for kb's graph. It turns notes and wiki content into a clustered knowledge graph.

kept.name: open-knowledge-format
kept.reason: Google's spec for knowledge stored as markdown plus frontmatter. It adds provenance and freshness fields, and it was noted as closely matching your wiki pattern.

kept.name: agentic-memory-benchmark
kept.reason: In this benchmark a plain, curated markdown wiki beat commercial memory products. That supports the markdown-notes approach.

kept.name: mcp-server-youtube-transcript
kept.reason: Fetches YouTube transcripts. It was saved specifically to cover video-to-markdown capture for the learning vault.

kept.name: claude-video
kept.reason: A /watch skill that pulls captions and frames from a video so Claude can turn it into grounded notes.

kept.name: vidnote
kept.reason: Converts video lectures into markdown with slide screenshots. It was saved for capturing courses, but it's rough and has a single maintainer.

kept.name: faster-whisper
kept.reason: Speech-to-text engine for videos that have no captions, part of the ingestion path.

kept.name: whisperx
kept.reason: Whisper transcription with word timestamps and speaker labels. Well suited to lecture and interview notes.

kept.name: markitdown
kept.reason: Microsoft's converter that turns PDFs, PPTX, Excel and other docs into markdown for saving as notes.

kept.name: mineru
kept.reason: Converts documents to markdown at several quality levels, with a searchable local document library. Useful for bulk ingestion.

kept.name: obsidian-skills
kept.reason: Skills for working with Obsidian notes. Includes Defuddle, which turns web pages into clean markdown.

kept.name: second-brain-skills
kept.reason: A 'second brain' skill collection for knowledge work. Close in spirit to the system you're describing.

kept.name: engram-learning-engine
kept.reason: A learning plugin with /learn, /review and /coach commands, spaced repetition and concept graphs. It's the nearest real match to a 'learn anything' skill.

kept.name: tutorial-creator
kept.reason: A skill for turning material into simple, clear tutorials to help you remember it. Fits 'simply explained'.

kept.name: claude-autoresearch
kept.reason: The catalog's text hit for 'learn anything' (it has a learn command). Note that no entry is actually named 'learn anything'.

kept.name: mit-opencourseware
kept.reason: Saved as source material for loading courses into the learning vault.

kept.name: karakeep
kept.reason: A self-hosted AI bookmark and knowledge manager with built-in agent skills. Another way to capture links and docs.

kept.name: tolvi
kept.reason: A vault for capturing decisions, as Claude Code skills. It overlaps with kb, so it's useful mainly for comparison.

kept.name: storybloq
kept.reason: A project-state, ticket and wiki tool. Close to tracking projects in a wiki, but it was set aside because it overlaps kb and has a non-commercial license.

kept.name: mex
